series.label: Net delta drift (PT delta − hedge, tokens)

notes: The PT has less than one token of delta before maturity (it trades at a discount) while the hedge is fixed at 1.0 per PT, so the book is net short early and converges to flat at maturity; this is the design, and the drift series shows it.

Deployment is chunked ($20k per hour) for HL book depth in the live design; the engine opens at once, which flatters nothing in a down-market window and slightly understates slippage in an up-market one.

At 1x the short is liquidated when ENA rises by roughly (1 + reserve/notional) above entry; the reserve is the only parameter that moves that line. A larger reserve earns nothing and lowers the yield on capital — the trade shown here.

series.label: Worst margin health by start date (100% = liquidation)

notes: A fixed yield locked at entry makes the base case positive by construction; what varies is funding, the rally-driven top-ups, and whether the reserve survives. Windows where it does not are the result to look at, and the reserve sweep is the design response.

A window holds the PT to the nearest maturity at or beyond 88 days from its start, or to the longest-dated market trading at the time when none reaches that far, so window lengths vary with Pendle's listing calendar.

notes: If a rally outruns margin + reserve the short is liquidated and the book is left long PT: the result then follows ENA's price, whatever its sign — the reserve is sized against this case, and the tiles show how much of it the +100% week used.

The one risk the hedge does not cover is the sENA/ENA exchange rate: the PT redeems sENA, the short is ENA. It is a property of the underlying rather than a parameter of the book, and it is run as a script in the repo rather than a page scenario (`--depeg`).

tables.title: Every overlap of two PT-sENA maturities in the data
tables.md:
| running PT | new listing | overlap (days) | running APY (median) | new APY (median) | gap needed to rotate | fired |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25 Sep 2025 | 27 Nov 2025 | 15 | 32.7% | 26.9% | +6.1% (at first overlap) | no |
| 27 Nov 2025 | 05 Feb 2026 | 19 | 26.7% | 22.9% | +4.8% (at first overlap) | no |
| 05 Feb 2026 | 30 Apr 2026 | 19 | 18.9% | 15.0% | +4.8% (at first overlap) | yes |
| 30 Apr 2026 | 24 Sep 2026 | 16 | 15.6% | 11.0% | +5.7% (at first overlap) | no |

Round-trip fee 25 bps of notional (2 × Pendle 8 bps + 2 × HL 4.5 bps); the rule rotates only when (new APY − running APY) × remaining horizon beats it.

notes: `gain_gt_fee` is the rule in the design: exit early only if (next_apy − cur_apy) × remaining horizon × notional beats the round-trip fee (2 × Pendle 8 bps + 2 × HL 4.5 bps). `single_print` rotates on any better print and pays the round-trip every time. `never` holds every PT to maturity.

Where the three rules agree it is because no new listing printed above the running PT during an overlap (the table): sENA maturities on Pendle list a few weeks before the previous one expires, and the expiring PT's implied APY runs up into maturity. The rule is live in the chain and checked daily; on this data it has nothing to fire on, which is itself the answer to 'why not roll early'.

sections.heading: What this is
sections.body_md:
dnENA: buy PT-sENA on Pendle at a discount, short the same token quantity of ENA on HyperCore at 1x, hold a 15% reserve in the HL account, top up margin from the reserve before liquidation, and hold to maturity — rolling only when the expected gain on a new maturity beats the round-trip fee. Return = the fixed yield locked at the PT discount + funding on the short − fees: the yield is known at entry, funding is the variable, delta is designed out token-for-token, and the margin is run defensively from the reserve.

```
q = (capital − reserve) / (pt_px·px + px/lev)        pt_qty = short_qty = q
implied APY = (1/pt_px)^(365/days) − 1              liq_px = (margin + q·px0) / (q·(1 + maint))
top up from reserve when equity/maintenance < 1.5     rotate iff (apy_next − apy_cur)·T·notional > round-trip fee
```

sections.heading: How to read the four families
sections.body_md:
1. **Actual window** — the published backtest page's Feb–Apr 2026 window reproduced from Pendle, HL and Binance data (its real-data result is kept as a tile; if the rebuilt number differs the page shows the rebuilt one).
2. **Rolling windows** — the same rules on every 88-day start date; the distribution is the result and the negative windows are the finding.
3. **Stresses** — one shock at a time, labelled as such: a +100% rally in a week (does the top-up rule hold, what idle capital does it cost), −20%/yr funding for a month (how much of the fixed yield it eats).
4. **Rotation** — the gain-over-fee rule against a single-print rule and against never rotating, on the same data: the design argument shown with numbers.

sections.heading: Reproduce
sections.body_md:
```
python -m strategies.dn_ena.fetch_data --from 2025-06-01    # Pendle PT-sENA history, HL ENA funding, Binance ENA spot
python -m strategies.dn_ena.backtest
python -m strategies.dn_ena.backtest --depeg             # the sENA/ENA depeg script (prints, no page)
```
`strategy.py` = sizing, margin, top-up, rotation rule; `backtest.py` = the engine and the four scenario families.
